Notice of Revised National Environmental Policy Act Implementing Procedures

data.abstract: The U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS or Department) is updating DHS Directive 023, Implementation of the National Environmental Policy Act, which establishes procedures for complying with the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA). This update is necessary in light of the recent rescission of the Council on Environmental Quality's NEPA implementing regulations, which DHS's procedures were designed to supplement. In addition, the update incorporates provisions from the Fixing America's Surface Transportation Act, the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act; and the Fiscal Responsibility Act of 2023 related to the environmental review process. The updated Directive promotes collaboration and efficiencies in the implementation of NEPA and modernizes the processes and procedures for environmental review. This update enables DHS to conduct coordinated, consistent, predictable, and timely environmental reviews, thus reducing unnecessary burdens and delays. The draft Directive is being made available for public review and comment. These comments will inform development of the final Directive. Upon finalization, the Directive will rescind DHS Directive 023-01, Rev 01 and DHS Instruction 023-01-001-01, Rev 01 which were issued in 2014.

items.title: Pacific Island Fisheries; Longline Retention Prohibition; Striped Marlin in the Western and Central Pacific Ocean North of the Equator

data.abstract: NMFS is prohibiting retention of Western and Central North Pacific Ocean (WCNPO) striped marlin (Kajikia audax) by vessels registered for use under a Hawaii longline limited access permit for the remainder of 2026 because the longline fishery has reached the 2026 longline retention limit. WCNPO stiped marlin are those caught in the Pacific Ocean north of the Equator (0[deg] latitude) and west of 150[deg] W longitude. This prohibition is intended to prevent the U.S. catch limit for WCNPO striped marlin from being exceeded and ensure compliance with NMFS regulations that implement decisions of the Western and Central Pacific Fisheries Commission (WCPFC).

items.title: Safety Zone; Mississippi River, New Orleans, LA

data.abstract: The Coast Guard is establishing a temporary safety zone for navigable waters on the Mississippi River near New Orleans, LA. The safety zone is needed to protect personnel, vessels, and the marine environment from potential hazards associated with the response to a vessel collision and sinking. Entry of vessels or persons into this zone is prohibited unless specifically authorized by the Captain of the Port, Sector New Orleans, or their designated representative.

items.title: Takes of Marine Mammals Incidental to Specified Activities; Taking Marine Mammals Incidental to Military Readiness Activities in the Mariana Islands Training and Testing Study Area

data.abstract: NMFS has received a request from the U.S. Department of the Navy (including the U.S. Navy and the U.S. Marine Corps; Navy) and on behalf of the U.S. Coast Guard (Coast Guard), U.S. Army (Army), and U.S. Air Force (Air Force) (hereafter, Navy, Coast Guard, Army, and Air Force are collectively referred to as the Action Proponents) for Incidental Take Regulations (ITR) and an associated Letter of Authorization (LOA) pursuant to the Marine Mammal Protection Act (MMPA). The requested regulations would govern the authorization of take of marine mammals incidental to training and testing activities and modernization and sustainment of ranges conducted in the Mariana Islands Training and Testing (MITT) Study Area over the course of 7 years from July 2027 through July 2034. NMFS requests comments on this proposed rule. NMFS will consider public comments prior to making any final decision on the promulgation of the requested ITR and issuance of the LOA; agency responses to public comments will be summarized in the final rule, if issued. The Action Proponents' activities are considered military readiness activities pursuant to the MMPA, as amended by the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2004 (2004 NDAA) and the NDAA for Fiscal Year 2019 (2019 NDAA).

Racial Nondiscrimination in Private Schools; Hearing

data.abstract: This document provides a notice of an additional date for the public hearing on the notice of proposed rulemaking (REG-119986-25) published in the Federal Register on Friday, September 4, 2026. The proposed regulations would provide that a private school is not described as an organization exempt from Federal income tax if it discriminates on the basis of race, color, or national or ethnic origin in administration of its educational, admissions, scholarship, athletic, or other policies, based on the fundamental public policy of the United States against such practices.

items.title: Automatic Enrollment Requirements Under Section 414A

data.abstract: This document sets forth final regulations that provide guidance with respect to the automatic enrollment requirements that apply to certain retirement plans. The regulations reflect statutory changes made by the SECURE 2.0 Act of 2022 requiring that certain cash or deferred arrangements and salary reduction agreements be eligible automatic contribution arrangements that satisfy additional specified requirements. The regulations affect participants in, beneficiaries of, employers maintaining, and administrators of certain retirement plans that include cash or deferred arrangements or annuity contracts purchased under salary reduction agreements and other retirement plans that include eligible automatic contribution arrangements.

items.title: Air Plan Approval; Virginia; Interstate Transport Requirements for the 2010 SO2 NAAQS

data.abstract: Pursuant to the Federal Clean Air Act (CAA or Act), the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is proposing to approve a State implementation plan (SIP) revision submitted by the Commonwealth of Virginia demonstrating that Virginia satisfies the interstate transport requirements of the CAA, for the 2010 1-hour sulfur dioxide (SO<INF>2</INF>) primary national ambient air quality standard (NAAQS). Specifically, the EPA proposes to find that the Virginia SIP contains adequate provisions prohibiting emissions from Commonwealth sources from contributing significantly to nonattainment or interfering with maintenance of the 2010 SO<INF>2</INF> NAAQS in any other State, consistent with the good neighbor provision of the CAA.
